title: I was rooting for the Tom Hanks / Kelli O’Hara romance though tbh #th...
transcript: Tom Hanks wrote a sci-fi romance play that he's also starring in. Based on a few of his short stories, Tom Hanks plays a time traveller from 2089 who goes back to the 1939 World's Fair and falls in love with a woman played by Kelli O'Hara. As a fan of time travel stories and of these actors, I was excited to see this. Overall I thought the play was….cute. Like, the concept is amusing, the execution is mostly inoffensive, but it doesn't leave much of an impact. It is kind of a romanticized nostalgia of that era, and there are some feeble attempts to subvert that or comment on it, but not enough to meaningfully avoid falling into that nostalgia p*rn trap. Like it was watchable enough. At least, scenes taking place in the past were; The future scenes are all written in this style that uses a lot of dense jargon for the wibbly wobbly timey wimey stuff. And maybe I'm just stupid, but these entire scenes played to me like total gibberish nonsense. Hanks at this like sci-fi tech company. I couldn't even tell what he did, or like if it was even the same company that did the time travel stuff. I really couldn't follow any of it. And ultimately it was kind of fine because it didn't impact the plot that much, but still, they spent a decent chunk of stage time on it. it also lessens the impact of the play in the sense that they lightly poke at this idea of Tom Hanks's character yearning to live in a world with more optimism. But without a coherent sense of the world that he's coming from, that yearning rings kind of hollow. They're also kind of lackadaisical about the rules of time travel in this world. Like, there are several allusions to potentially negative consequences, but they never even really follow through on it, which just makes it feel even more like they put a sci-fi skin on Tom Hanks's candy floss nostalgia fantasy. This is Tom Hanks's first stage role in about seven years and first one in New York in, like, almost 13 years. And the role he wrote for himself here is suited to his strengths in the sense that he's playing this warm, likable guy. But, like, he's a very skilled Oscar winning actor. And it feels like he played it very safe here. And especially in a rare return to the stage in this passion project, you'd think he'd wanna stretch himself a little more. But still, it was a solidly charming performance. So if you're interested and able to see it, This World of Tomorrow is running at the Shed in New York City through December 21st.
classificationReason: Reviews a Tom Hanks play with Kelli O'Hara about time travel, but this show is not on the provided list
reasoning: The reviewer uses lukewarm language throughout ('cute,' 'mostly inoffensive,' 'kind of fine') and identifies significant flaws while acknowledging some positives. They neither recommend nor discourage attendance, presenting a balanced but unenthusiastic assessment.
